title: One-record iteration cannot assume a size-hinted batch contains one line
applies_when: Reviewing Python file-like wrappers whose next/__next__ implementation calls readlines(hint) and returns only the first element; especially buffered streams and consecutive empty lines.
lesson: A readlines hint is a byte/character size hint, not a line count. readlines(1) can consume two newline-only lines before exceeding its hint; returning only the first silently drops the other. Use readline() for a one-line iterator, or retain every consumed batch member. Probe the actual buffered and raw wrappers with consecutive empty lines, bare CR/CRLF, final partial lines and EOF. Check both the returned sequence and the remaining stream position; a normal multi-byte first line alone masks the error.
avoid_when: Do not transfer this rule to APIs that explicitly define their argument as a record count. Binary and text newline rules differ. Fixing iterator consumption does not establish complete readlines size-hint conformance, distributed-backend parity, performance, or upstream acceptance.

evidence.note: The file-like interface defines hint in bytes/characters, not number of lines; binary readline terminates on a newline byte. This is an API contract, not performance evidence.
File.next delegates to readline instead of consuming readlines(1) and discarding all but its first element.

The published reproduction includes buffered/unbuffered consecutive-empty-line iteration. The author reports matched focused SQLite/libjfs tests (previous head 59/60, fixed 60/60); this is not independent maintainer CI or the full metadata-engine matrix.
